what_it_does: Manufacturing imperfections create tiny random variations in transistor properties—like building millions of identical resistors that are all slightly different. Traditional chip testing looks for obvious failures (stuck signals, broken wires), but misses timing failures caused by unlucky combinations of many small variations affecting different transistors simultaneously. This work proposes testing strategies that specifically target transistor variations: instead of testing for single broken components, tests are designed to catch timing errors from correlated multi-device variations in how fast transistors can switch.
